question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{25}$ be a random sample of size $n=25$ from a population with probability density function 

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}{x}^{2}, & 0\le x\le 2, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.15,$ calculate $P(\overset{―}{X}>1.6).$

*Hint: Assume that the sample size is sufficiently large for the central limit theorem to be applied. A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ | $\,0.09\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.1\,$ | $\,0.8790\,$ | $\,0.8810\,$ | $\,0.8830\,$ |
| $\,1.2\,$ | $\,0.8980\,$ | $\,0.8997\,$ | $\,0.9015\,$ |
| $\,1.3\,$ | $\,0.9147\,$ | $\,0.9162\,$ | $\,0.9177\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =25,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}x\cdot \frac{3}{8}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}\frac{3}{8}{x}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{3{x}^{4}}{32}]}_{0}^{2} \\  & =\frac{3}{2} \\  & =1.5,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.15.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(1.5,\frac{0.15}{25}) \\  & ∼N(1.5,0.006).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>1.6).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>1.6) & =P(Z>\frac{1.6-1.5}{\sqrt{0.006}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>1.29)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the complement of the normal distribution, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Z>1.29) & =1-P(Z<1.29) \\  & =1-Φ(1.29).\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
Φ(1.29)=0.9015.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>1.6) & =1-Φ(1.29) \\  & =1-0.9015 \\  & =0.0985.\end{aligned}
$$
